# Fitz Hawksmoor

## Description
A neat, flour-dusted man of fifty in a leather apron over a lord's coat, with a pencil
behind each ear and a rolled plan under one arm at all times. Speaks in precise,
complete sentences while pastry cools behind him. Has a griffon called Marchpane who
sleeps across the kitchen door like a very large draught excluder.

## Personality & motivation
Methodical, proud, lonely, and absolutely sure that any problem can be drawn. He built
a castle that flies; it flew; the harpies moved in before he could land it; he has
been baking a pie large enough to tempt them out ever since this morning. He wants his
castle back and someone to show it to. He would never leave it. He will give anything
in it to whoever makes the singing stop, except Marchpane.

## Knowledge & secrets
- Freely shares: the castle's workings (the helm in the gatehouse; it will not answer while the song plays, "resonance, I expect"); the layout; that the harpies' nest is in the music room among the eggs and "there is a stone in it that hums; they fight over it; I assume it is the trouble"; the password for the gargoyles ("pie"); his plan, in full, with drawings
- Needs persuasion (DC 12): the castle's circuit is fixed and he did not set it; it passes the ridge at 14:00 "as if it wanted to be caught"; the ladder is his, he lowers it every pass hoping for a baker
- Needs trust: Marchpane will carry two people, once, down to the ridge; and if the Song is taken out of the castle he can steer, and will put the castle down "in the Keep's courtyard, since the King keeps asking me to supper"

He does not sleep tonight; he does not know why he is not tired.
